key_insight: Selective LLM assistance achieved 83.19% locked-test ICD-10 accuracy while invoking the LLM for only 31.97% of diagnoses.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more efficient ICD-10 coding from short, noisy diagnosis text, though clinical workflow benefits remain untested.
method: Generate code candidates using transformer embeddings and tree-based supervised models.
Rerank candidates and selectively invoke an LLM for uncertain cases.
Fuse predictions in the final Pre-LLM fusion system.
evidence_signal: With out-of-fold model selection and a locked test set sharing no source-file groups, accuracy rose from 74.32% for the supervised baseline to 83.19%, a 34.5% relative error reduction.
watch_item: Generalizability across institutions and coding practices is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Call-Efficient ICD-10 Code Prediction via Supervised Candidate Generation and Selective LLM Invocation
